text.p: An expert panel commissioned by India's central bank has charted a road-map to make the rupee fully convertible on the capital account by the year 2000. The panel has set ambitious fiscal and macroeconomic targets, but the move towards freeing the rupee spells major changes in India's financial sector.
Reuters specialist correspondents in Bombay and Delhi talked to bankers, analysts and economists to gauge how the drive for convertibility will impact upon the Indian economy.
In the second of the reports, Bombay's Shyam Kumar looks at the shakeout in Indian banking that is likely to result from full rupee convertibility.
